description: A four-lane shift register for control voltages: one voltage goes in and four come out, each a delayed or recirculated version of it, with its own buffer length, clock division and mode

params.text: Sets that lane's buffer length, 0 to 16; in parallel mode that is how many lane clocks of delay, and in cascade mode how long the loop is
Switches that lane between a delay line fed from the input and a loop fed one value at a time from the lane above it
Divides that lane's clock by 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 8, slowing both its reads and its writes, which multiplies with the buffer length
Clears every buffer, every held voltage, the jumble pick and all the counters on each press

inputs.text: The voltage the lanes carry, sampled each time a lane fires
Each rise advances every lane and is also the root of the cascade chain
Changes every lane's buffer length at once, ±5V for ±15 steps, added to each lane's own knob on top of its own step CV
A rise clears every buffer, every held voltage, the jumble pick and all the counters
Changes that lane's buffer length, ±5V for ±15 steps, added to that lane's knob

outputs.text: A gate on each of that lane's firings, following the shape of the clock going in
A voltage picked at random from the four lanes' held values, drawn again on every clock
A gate following the shape of the clock going in, to go with the random pick beside it

notes: pulling the CV cable does not silence the module: each lane keeps cycling through a sixteen-slot history of what it has already heard, so it carries on playing out of what it was fed
cascade mode on the first lane has no lane above it to draw from, so that lane falls back to parallel; its mode switch is left off the panel for that reason
menu: Clear all — wipes every buffer, every held voltage, the jumble pick and all the counters, which is what a reset does
